facts_of_case: Petitioner-husband and respondent-wife filed a petition under Section 13-B of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 for decree of divorce by mutual consent. The trial court dismissed their petition. Both parties decided to dissolve their marriage by mutual consent during the pendency of the appeal.

legal_principles.principle: Waiver of statutory period is allowed when parties are still ready and willing to part ways by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent.
legal_principles.held: Since, the petition is filed by both the parties for seeking decree of divorce by way of mutual consent and that both the parties are still ready and willing to part ways by way of decree of divorce by mutual consent, therefore, present application is allowed and the statutory period of six months under Section 13-B of the Act is hereby waived off.

legal_principles.principle: Parties' agreement to dissolve marriage by mutual consent can be reduced into writing and taken on record.
legal_principles.held: The parties have also entered into an agreement which was reduced into writing on 08.04.2019 (Annexure A-1) which bears the signatures of both the parties.
applicable_acts_sections: Order 6 Rule 17 read with Section 151 of CPC

outcome.final_order: The statutory period of six months under Section 13-B of the Act was waived off, and the main appeal was taken on board today itself.

use_for_drafting: drafting a petition for divorce by mutual consent
seeking pre-ponement of hearing in a family court
waiving the mandatory period for grant of decree of divorce
